title: Quantum hardware startup Planckian awarded €10m EIC funding under accelerator program
html:
Quantum hardware firm Planckian has been selected by the European Innovation Council (EIC) for its EIC Accelerator, which will see the company awarded a €2.5 million ($2.7m) grant, in addition to a €7.5 million ($8.2m) EIC equity investment.

The grant will fund a 24-month program that the company said will result in a quantum computer that is market-ready. Planckian was one of 35 companies selected for the accelerator.

“Every superconducting quantum computer built so far pays the same tax: each new qubit means more cables, more electronics, and more cost,” said Michele Dallari, co-founder and CEO of Planckian. “Our architecture is designed to break that link. The EIC’s backing lets us take it from the lab to a system that external users can run.”

Founded in 2023 as a spin-out from the University of Pisa and the Scuola Normale Superiore, Planckian builds quantum processors that allow multiple qubits to share control lines, reducing wiring complexity while bypassing the limits of conventional chip architectures.

The startup said that this approach enables a “new generation of quantum computing systems” that have been designed to scale from the outset.

In September 2026, Planckian was the only Italian company from a cohort of 13 selected to participate in the EuroHPC Quantum Grand Challenge. In Phase I, the firm was awarded €300,000 ($328,700) to develop a technical and financial roadmap for scaling its quantum computing architecture.
summary: Italian firm developing quantum processors that utilize shared control lines
